First, we differentiate both sides of the equation with respect to $x,$ assuming that $y=y(x).$

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{y}^{3}+\operatorname{cos}⁡(y)-2{x}^{2} & =5 \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({y}^{3}+\operatorname{cos}⁡(y)-2{x}^{2}) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(5) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({y}^{3})+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(y))-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2{x}^{2}) & =0 \\ 3{y}^{2}(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x})-\operatorname{sin}⁡(y)(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x})-4x & =0\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now we solve the equation for $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}(3{y}^{2}-\operatorname{sin}⁡(y)) & =4x \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{4x}{3{y}^{2}-\operatorname{sin}⁡(y)}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
